Name: binding_scope_leakage_ladder
Title: Global Fact, Scene Table, or Instance Replay: The Scope of Instance Bindings Sets How Much of a Memory Gain Is Near-Duplicate Leakage and Whether a Static Prompt Can Match It
Short Hypothesis: An experience bank helps on a new task instance only through information that transfers from bank items to that instance. The scope of the instance bindings (global = per object class, per scene, per instance) fixes both the smallest static substitute for retrieval and the share of the retrieval gain that is near-duplicate leakage: at class scope one sentence per class matches scene-query retrieval and one bank item per class suffices; at scene scope one static (scene, class) table matches it; at instance scope no static prefix smaller than one row per instance exists, the gain exists only through the instance's own duplicate, it is linear in the duplicate rate because other games' duplicates do not spill over to non-duplicated instances and the duplicate is followed even when the trajectories retrieved beside it contradict it, and a whole-bank prefix that contains the duplicate cannot replace the query. The natural ALFWorld bank sits at class scope (unseen >= seen), so its measured +17.2 net residual over the best static arm (static3) compiles into about 20 class-location sentences.
Related Work: Evo-Memory (arXiv:2511.20857) and ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) measure memory as test-time evolution over task streams without reporting how much of the gain comes from near-duplicate tasks within the stream. EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421) organizes memory by scope (in-episode vs cross-episode) and content, and finds long-context baselines outperform memory methods, but does not manipulate binding scope or duplicate rate. AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams with transfer-gain metrics, without a compiled-prompt arm or a scope manipulation. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316) draws related tasks from dependency links (observed relatedness). The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows adoption of wrong retrieved memory. In the home literature, deduplication of training data (arXiv:2107.06499) and contamination analyses (ConTAM arXiv:2411.03923; rephrased-sample contamination arXiv:2311.04850) quantify score inflation from near-duplicate overlap for pretraining, never for experience banks. Archived order_randomized_leakage_audit audited leakage by order randomization (observed); Measurements A and C (unseen >= seen; k3 - static3 = +17.2 net at the natural bank) are the starting point.
Abstract: Memory benchmarks differ in what an experience bank can transfer to a new instance: a rule that holds everywhere (per object class), a binding that holds within a scene, or a binding that holds only for the instance itself, which the bank contains only if the instance recurs. We manipulate this scope on ALFWorld with the relocation machinery (target objects moved off their canonical receptacle, 25-step budget) under three relocation rules: global (every instance of a class goes to one receptacle type in every scene), scene (per (scene, class)), instance (per game). Supply is the fraction s of eval games whose scope unit is covered in the bank: at scene scope s in {0, 1} (same-scene relocated sibling present or not); at instance scope s in {0, 0.5, 1}, where the duplicate is the PDDL expert's trajectory for the eval game's own relocated init, so every game carries one independent of any baseline outcome; at global scope the full relocated bank versus a 20-item one-per-class bank. Arms per scope: scene-query retrieval k=3; the reference static arm static3-relocated (three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars rebuilt from the relocated bank; Measurement C's best static arm); the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt; the scope's compiled static arm (one sentence per class at global scope; one static prefix holding every (scene, class) row at scene scope; none at instance scope, where no prefix smaller than one row per instance exists); and the whole-bank arm (20 items in context at global scope; the scene-restricted bank, <= 80 items in fixed order, at scene and instance scope). At instance scope two neighbour-controlled arms hold the duplicate at rank 1 and fix ranks 2-3 by rule: conflict (two same-scene, same-class trajectories that put the class elsewhere) and neutral (two same-scene trajectories of another class). Every retrieval number is reported minus static3-relocated and minus the best static arm on the same (game, seed), with cached and uncached prefill tokens. The leakage index at a scope is the part of the retrieval residual removed by deleting scope-matched duplicates; at instance scope the s=0.5 condition is run as two complementary draws so that the residual on non-duplicated games N(0.5) has the full n. A natural-bank anchor cell tests whether Measurement C's +17.2 residual over static3 compiles into a class-location table. Predictions: a sentence matches retrieval at class scope, a row table at scene scope, nothing but the duplicate at instance scope; N(0.5) equals the s=0 residual (no spillover) and the conflict arm matches the neutral arm (no discounting of a contradicted duplicate); an 80-item whole bank that contains the duplicate loses >= 14 net to the query at instance scope; each prediction names the cell that can refute it.
Experiments: 1. Gate (pre-registered, the positive control shared with the relocation design): scene scope, s=1, relocated x 25-step: scene-query retrieval minus static3-relocated >= +14 net; if it fails the ladder is not run and the failure is reported. 2. Construction: three relocation rules applied to the PDDL init of the 274 eval games and of the train games in eval scenes; expert trajectories regenerated with the ALFWorld PDDL expert (CPU); instance-scope duplicates are the expert trajectories of the eval games' own relocated inits, placed in the bank for a fraction s of games (s=0.5 as two complementary seed-drawn halves A and B); static3-relocated is rebuilt per scope from the relocated bank with the same three exemplar slots as Measurement C; the compiled sentence and table are written by rule from the bank; eval games sharing (goal text, scene) with another eval game are counted and form the tied subset; neighbour-controlled contexts at instance scope s=1 are built by rule from the same-scene bank (conflict: the two lowest-game-id items whose task targets the eval game's object class and whose instance relocation puts it on a receptacle other than the duplicate's; neutral: the two lowest-game-id items targeting another class; games with fewer than two conflict candidates are filled by the neutral rule and counted), rendered in the k=3 retrieval slot format, uncached. 3. Natural-bank anchor (1 cell): class-location table static (one sentence per class listing the receptacles where that class was picked in the natural train bank, <= 430 tokens, cached), paired against Measurement C's k3 and static3 rows on the same (game, seed) under Measurement C settings (k3 re-run as one extra cell if the vLLM build changed). 4. Confirmatory cells, each 274 games x 2 seeds = 548 episodes: scene scope (6): retrieval s=1, retrieval s=0, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, table static, whole-bank; global scope (6): retrieval full bank, retrieval 20-item bank, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, compiled sentence, whole-bank-20; instance scope (9): retrieval s=1, s=0.5 draw A, s=0.5 draw B, s=0, conflict-neighbour s=1, neutral-neighbour s=1, static3-relocated, type-agnostic, whole-bank. 5. Exploratory (2 cells): on-policy self-duplicate at instance scope s=1 (the game's own verified success from the type-agnostic cell, which doubles as the first pass; solved games only) versus the expert duplicate; stale duplicate (the same game's canonical pre-relocation expert trajectory) at instance scope s=1. Logged without episodes: rank of the self-duplicate under scene-query and goal-query; per-episode retrieval composition at ranks 1-3 (own duplicate, other eval duplicate, train item; same class or not; target receptacle agrees or conflicts with the duplicate's). 6. Arithmetic: 22 confirmatory + 2 exploratory (+1 optional k3 re-run) = 24-25 cells x 548 = 13.2k-13.7k episodes; at Measurement C's throughput (~19 episodes/min on two A100s, one vLLM replica per GPU) about 11.5-12 h, static cells faster because their prefixes are cached. 7. Cost: cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode; accuracy-cost curve per scope.
Baselines and Ablations: Static (cached, byte-identical prefixes): static3-relocated (reference static arm at every scope; three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars rebuilt from each scope's relocated bank, ~430 tokens); type-agnostic six-procedure prompt (no bindings; run at every scope, controls type conditioning); compiled sentence per class (global scope, ~20 sentences); compiled (scene, class) table as one static prefix (scene scope, <= 274 rows); class-location table (natural bank); whole-bank: the 20-item one-per-class bank in context at global scope, the scene-restricted bank at scene and instance scope (all bank items from the eval game's scene, <= 80 in fixed game-id order, the eval game's own duplicate included at instance scope s=1; banks over 80 items drop train items by highest game id first and counts are reported). Retrieval: scene-query k=3 (goal plus first observation), the Measurement C retriever; ablations: 20-item one-per-class bank versus the full relocated bank at global scope; s=0 at scene and instance scope (scope-matched duplicates deleted); s=0.5 in two complementary draws at instance scope; neighbour-controlled contexts at instance scope s=1 (duplicate at rank 1, ranks 2-3 fixed by rule: conflict = two same-scene, same-class items relocating the class elsewhere; neutral = two same-scene items of another class; same slot format and token count as k=3, uncached), which manipulate the only channel through which anything but the duplicate can move a duplicate-present game; stale and on-policy duplicates at instance scope (exploratory). Per the rules every retrieval cell is reported minus static3-relocated and minus the best static arm of its scope (max over the static arms above by pooled success). Dropped from earlier versions: the global s=0 cell (P3 carries the global leakage claim), the k=1 and k=7 sweeps, and the random-type length placebo (Measurement C's blind1 bounds the length effect at -3 net).
Falsifiable Predictions: Margins follow the brief: the +-8 net floor at 274 x 2 is the smallest reportable difference and +14 is the confirmatory margin. P0 (natural-bank anchor, stated against Measurement C's k3 - static3 = +17.2 [+11.9, +22.4]) The class-location table static minus k3 >= -8 net on the natural bank, i.e. the table recovers at least +9 of the +17.2 over static3. Falsified by table - k3 < -8 in the anchor cell (the +17.2 is scene-family information a class sentence cannot carry; the natural bank then sits between class and scene scope). P1 (gate) At scene scope, s=1, retrieval minus static3-relocated >= +14 net. Falsified by < +8 in that cell; the ladder is then not run. P2 (class scope compiles to a sentence) Positive control read first: at global scope retrieval (full bank) minus static3-relocated >= +14, falsified by < +8 (the reader does not carry a class rule out of other-scene trajectories), in which case P2 and P3 are reported as not testable. P2 proper: compiled-sentence static minus retrieval >= -8 net. Falsified by sentence < retrieval - 8 in the sentence cell (the reader applies a concrete trajectory but not a stated rule). P3 (one item per class suffices) At global scope retrieval with the 20-item bank is within +-8 of retrieval with the full relocated bank. Falsified by 20-item < full - 8 in the 20-item cell (a many-shot per-class requirement). P4 (scene scope compiles to a table) Table static minus retrieval (s=1) >= -8 net at scene scope. Falsified by table < retrieval - 8 in the table cell (the reader cannot look up its scene's row among <= 274). P5 (instance scope: an exact duplicate is replayed) At instance scope, retrieval (s=1, expert self-duplicate present) minus static3-relocated >= +28 net. Falsified by < +20 (95% CI excluding +28) in that cell (the reader does not follow even its own instance's expert trajectory within 25 steps, or k=3 does not rank it first). P6 (headline: the instance-scope gain is the duplicate and nothing else) Read if residual(1) >= +14. Two branches, each with a manipulated pair. (a) No spillover: at instance scope s=0.5, pooled over the two complementary draws so the term has n = 274 x 2, the residual on games whose duplicate is absent, N(0.5), is <= residual(0) + 8. Falsified by N(0.5) >= residual(0) + 14 (other games' duplicates in the bank seed a search strategy that transfers to non-duplicated games; s=0.5 cells against the s=0 cell). residual(0) is a measured anchor, not a claim. (b) No discounting of a contradicted duplicate: at instance scope s=1, the conflict-neighbour arm (own duplicate at rank 1, two same-scene, same-class trajectories that put the class on another receptacle at ranks 2-3) minus the neutral-neighbour arm (same rank 1, two same-scene other-class trajectories) >= -8 net. Falsified by conflict <= neutral - 14 (the reader visits a neighbour's receptacle or hedges between trajectories and runs out of the 25 steps, so the duplicate's value depends on what is retrieved beside it; conflict cell against the neutral cell). D(0.5) against residual(1) is reported descriptively, conditioned on the logged rank-2/3 composition, not as a claim: a duplicate-present game sees its duplicate at rank 1 at either s and the bank's rate is invisible to the reader. Pooled residual(s) = s x D(s) + (1 - s) x N(s) is an identity; slope and intercept over s are reported descriptively. P7 (the whole bank does not replace the query at instance scope) At instance scope s=1, the scene-restricted whole-bank arm (<= 80 items, the game's own duplicate among them) <= retrieval - 14 net. Falsified by whole-bank >= retrieval - 8 in that cell (the reader finds its own instance among 80 same-scene trajectories without a query). Shared terms: P5 and P7 use the instance-scope s=1 retrieval cell, which also gates P6; P6(a) is decided by the s=0.5 and s=0 cells and P6(b) by the conflict and neutral cells, none of which enters P5 or P7; P1 and P4 share the scene-scope s=1 retrieval cell; P2 and P3 share the global full-bank cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Task success on identical (game, seed) pairs across arms within each scope; paired nets with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples) and 95% CIs; the +-8 net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin, +14 the confirmatory margin (half the Gate-0 gain), and P5 uses +28 with its falsifier at +20 so that a 14-point loss in P6(b) is a reportable loss. The reference static arm is pre-registered as static3-relocated per scope; retrieval minus the best static arm of the scope is also reported for every cell. The s=0.5 draws are complementary halves of the 274 games, so N(0.5) and D(0.5) are each measured on every game once at each seed (n = 274 x 2, floor +-8) and do not depend on which games carry duplicates; the same expert duplicates are used in every instance-scope arm. The conflict and neutral arms differ only in the two rank-2/3 items (same rank-1 duplicate, same slot format, matched token count); the per-episode composition of retrieved ranks 1-3 is logged in every retrieval cell (own duplicate, other eval duplicate, train item; same class; receptacle agrees or conflicts with the duplicate's) and D(0.5) - residual(1) is reported conditioned on it. Eval games tied on (goal text, scene) with another eval game are counted; the primary instance-scope analysis is on untied games and the tied subset is reported separately. Same decoding, vLLM build, prompt template and retriever as Measurement C; static prefixes byte-identical with cache hits verified from logs; cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode logged. Gate and P0-P7 pre-registered before the first confirmatory cell; per-type claims exploratory; valid_seen and valid_unseen reported separately and pooled.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The ladder depends on the relocation positive control; if no binding-bound residual over static3-relocated exists at scene scope the design yields the gate failure and the natural-bank anchor only. Expert self-duplicates are off-policy (the PDDL expert's action sequence, not the reader's), so P5 may overstate what a self-pool memory would supply; the on-policy exploratory cell bounds this on solved games. At instance scope, eval games tied on (goal, scene) can retrieve a sibling's duplicate with a different relocation; the tied subset is reported separately and reduces n for the primary analysis. The conflict arm needs two same-scene, same-class items with a different target receptacle; games with fewer are filled by the neutral rule and counted, and if more than a quarter of games are affected P6(b) is reported on the fully-conflicting subset with its reduced n. The neighbour-controlled arms are constructed contexts, not retriever outputs, so they bound the effect of contradicting neighbours rather than reproduce the retriever's own mixture, which is logged. Global-scope relocation to a single receptacle type per class may be impossible for some (scene, class) pairs (receptacle absent); those games are dropped with counts. The compiled sentence and table are written by rule, favouring the compiled arms relative to model-written playbooks. The instance-scope static substitute is defined as a prefix whose size does not grow with the number of instances; the O(instances) duplicate-row table is the whole-bank arm in row form and is not run. The whole-bank arm at scene and instance scope is scene-restricted (the stated truncation rule), so it is conditioned on scene identity though not on the goal. Scope is manipulated on one environment; the cross-environment claim that a bank statistic (binding scope entropy) predicts the residual is a follow-up on WebShop, not measured here. Two seeds only.
Addresses gap: G10 (how much of the benefit of experience retrieval depends on task relatedness or near-duplication within the stream, with token cost and scaling with memory size unreported): the duplicate rate and the binding scope are manipulated, the leakage share is measured against the compiled static arms and the best static arm, cached/uncached token cost per scope is logged, and bank size is varied (20 items versus the full bank at global scope; an 80-item whole bank versus k=3 at instance scope).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Measurement A: unseen approximately equal to seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': Measurement C shows retrieval beats the type-conditioned static3 by +17.2, so the value is not the type's procedure; this idea claims it is a class-scope location prior that compiles into about 20 sentences (P0), and that the seen-unseen gap is a leakage index that the binding scope moves from zero (class scope) to the whole retrieval residual (instance scope), which the bullet does not state. Digest card arxiv:2511.20857 (Evo-Memory): this idea claims the stream gain at instance scope is the duplicate and nothing else (no spillover to non-duplicated instances, no discounting of a duplicate that its retrieved neighbours contradict, no static substitute smaller than the duplicates, no whole-bank replacement of the query), while at class scope one sentence substitutes and one item per class suffices; that card measures none of this because the duplicate rate within its streams is neither controlled nor reported. Archived order_randomized_leakage_audit observed leakage by reordering; here the scope and rate of duplicates and the content retrieved beside a duplicate are manipulated, and the duplicates are constructed independently of the reader's own outcomes.
Changes made: Second pass; only P6 was flagged (near_entailed). P6(b), the discount branch: was D(0.5) against residual(1); the check is right that a duplicate-present game sees its duplicate at rank 1 at both s and never sees the bank's rate, so only the uncontrolled rank-2/3 content could move it. Replaced by the check's third fix, a claim about retrieved-neighbour content with a manipulated pair: two constructed instance-scope s=1 arms, conflict (duplicate at rank 1 plus two same-scene, same-class trajectories relocating the class elsewhere) and neutral (duplicate plus two same-scene other-class trajectories); claim conflict - neutral >= -8, falsified by conflict <= neutral - 14 in the conflict cell. The check's second fix is taken as well: per-episode retrieval composition at ranks 1-3 is logged in every retrieval cell and D(0.5) - residual(1) is reported conditioned on it, as a descriptive number and no longer a claim. The check's first fix (fill ranks 2-3 from the same items at s=1 and s=0.5) was refused because it makes D(0.5) = residual(1) true by construction. P6(a), the spillover branch (N(0.5) against residual(0)), is unchanged and was already open. The linear-in-s identity is stated as an identity and reported descriptively, not as a test. Shared terms: P6 no longer reads residual(1) except as its read gate; its two branches are decided by cells that enter neither P5 nor P7. Cells: +2 (instance scope 9), 24-25 cells x 548 = 13.2k-13.7k episodes, about 11.5-12 h on two A100s. P0-P5 and P7 unchanged, no margin lowered. Novelty: the no-discounting claim is sharper than before, since it now says the duplicate is followed against two explicit contradictions rather than under an invisible rate change, and it can fail by a named mechanism (the reader visits a neighbour's receptacle inside the 25-step budget).
